subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Find the lengths of the normal and the subnormal at a point on the curve y = (a/2)(e^(x/a) + e^(−x/a)).

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say what dy/dx is, what 1 + (dy/dx)² simplifies to on this curve, and the formulas for the length of the normal and the subnormal.

steps.label: Differentiate the curve
steps.margin_note: First mark. The chain rule gives +1/a from the first exponential and −1/a from the second, so the sum in y becomes a difference in dy/dx. The a outside cancels with the 1/a inside.

steps.why: Both lengths asked for are built from y and dy/dx, so the derivative comes first. The a/2 outside and the 1/a from the chain rule cancel to 1/2, which is why the derivative is simpler than the curve.
common_mistakes: Differentiating e⁻ˣ⁄ᵃ to +(1/a)e⁻ˣ⁄ᵃ and keeping a plus sign between the two terms.
Leaving the factor a/2 in dy/dx instead of cancelling it to 1/2.
Treating a as a variable and differentiating it as well.
steps.memory_tip: The curve has a plus between the exponentials, the derivative has a minus. One differentiation swaps the sign.

steps.label: Show that 1 + m² = y²/a²
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Both lengths carry a √(1 + m²), so simplifying it once here does the work for both. The +1, written as (1/4) × 4, adds 4 inside the bracket and turns the −2 into +2 and completes the perfect square.

recall.must_convey: That 1 + m² collapses to (1/4)(eˣ⁄ᵃ + e⁻ˣ⁄ᵃ)², which is y²/a².

steps.why: The formulas for both the normal and the subnormal contain √(1 + m²), and on this curve that root has an exact simple value. Doing the simplification once, before either formula is used, keeps the last two steps to one line each.
common_mistakes: Expanding (eˣ⁄ᵃ − e⁻ˣ⁄ᵃ)² without the middle term −2.
Forgetting to write 1 as 4/4 before adding, and losing the +2.
Writing eˣ⁄ᵃ + e⁻ˣ⁄ᵃ = y/a instead of 2y/a.
steps.memory_tip: The square of a difference has −2 in the middle; adding 1 = (1/4) × 4 adds 4 inside the bracket, changing −2 to +2, which gives the square of the sum. That is the simplification used here.

steps.label: Length of the normal
steps.margin_note: Third mark. State the formula before substituting. y is positive everywhere on this curve and a > 0, so the square root is y/a with no sign to worry about.

recall.must_convey: That length of the normal = y√(1 + m²) = y(y/a) = y²/a.

steps.why: The length of the normal is the distance from the point to the x-axis measured along the normal, and the factor √(1 + m²) is what stretches y along that slanted line. On this curve that factor is y/a exactly.
common_mistakes: Using the length of the tangent formula, which divides by m as well.
Writing √(y²/a²) as y²/a² — the root removes the squares, so the factor is y/a; only multiplying by y afterwards gives y²/a.
Giving the subnormal ym here instead of the length of the normal y√(1 + m²).
steps.memory_tip: Length of the normal = y√(1 + m²); the length of the tangent is the same thing divided by m. The normal has no m in the denominator.

steps.label: Length of the subnormal
steps.margin_note: Fourth mark. The subnormal is the product y·m, and here that product is a difference of squares: (P + Q)(P − Q) with P = eˣ⁄ᵃ and Q = e⁻ˣ⁄ᵃ.
lines: Length of the subnormal = y · m

lines.text: ((a/4)(e²ˣ⁄ᵃ − e⁻²ˣ⁄ᵃ) is negative when x < 0, so the
length of the subnormal is its modulus)

recall.must_convey: That the subnormal is ym, and the product of the sum and the difference gives (a/4)(e²ˣ⁄ᵃ − e⁻²ˣ⁄ᵃ).
accept: the subnormal is y times dy by dx
sum times difference gives a difference of squares
the subnormal is a by four into e power two x by a minus e power minus two x by a
subnormal ante y into m
the two brackets multiply to give the squared exponents
a by two times half is a by four

steps.why: The subnormal is the horizontal distance from the foot of the ordinate to the point where the normal cuts the x-axis, and it equals y·dy/dx. The two brackets are a sum and a difference of the same pair, so their product removes the cross terms.
common_mistakes: Dividing instead of multiplying, which gives the subtangent y/m.
Expanding the product term by term and keeping the two cross terms that cancel.
Writing the coefficient as a/2 instead of a/4.
steps.memory_tip: Subtangent divides, subnormal multiplies: y/m and ym. The word with more letters, subtangent, is the one that DIVIDES.
lines_compact: Length of the subnormal = y · m

insider_note: The derivative is the difference of the two exponentials over 2, and 1 + m² then becomes a perfect square. That is what lets the root be taken cleanly.
